text:
alex: Heads-up — we just saw GPU nodepool provisioning hit soft limits in us-west1-b. Several pending pods are stuck Pending due to quota/zone capacity. Any quick mitigation ideas?
maya: Ugh, saw the alerts. Is this the spot/preemptible pool or the reserved pool?
alex: Mostly spot. Reserved pool still has a small buffer but we can't push high-priority infer jobs there without risking latency SLOs.
sam: Can we do cross-zone spillover to us-west1-c? Cluster autoscaler should be able to scale a different nodepool, but we need taint/toleration and topologySpread considerations.
carla: Also need to check image pull network egress — last time cross-zone nodes had long InitContainer pulls because our mirror wasn't in that zone.
alex: Good call. Current error from the Pending pods: `0/12 nodes are available: 12 Insufficient nvidia-t4-gpu.`
jin: What about short-term soft-fallback to a CPU-only fallback for low-priority batch jobs? We could mark them best-effort and run with fewer GPUs.
maya: We have two classes: realtime inference (P0) and batch rerank (P2). Realtime must stay on GPU. Batch we can demote to CPU for now.
sam: For GPUs we have two levers: 1) autoscale up different AZ nodepool (us-west1-c) with same GPU type, 2) fallback to smaller GPU (e.g., t4 -> v100?) — but model compatibility + quantization concerns.
carla: Also cost tradeoff: switching to on-demand from spot will triple hourly costs. Need explicit approval from finance for extended period.
oncall-ops: k8s-autoscaler-bot reports: `HorizontalClusterAutoscaler: scaling blocked by cloud quota in us-west1-b; recommended target: +8 nodes in us-west1-c`
alex: Can we patch nodeSelector/Tolerations at the Deployment level dynamically to allow scheduling to the us-west1-c pool?
sam: We use nodeAffinity to pin realtime pods to nodepool GPUs with label `gpu.family=t4`. If we create a new nodepool in us-west1-c with same label it should accept them without code changes. Need to create nodepool first.
maya: I'll open a short-lived nodepool with `gcloud` now: ```gcloud container node-pools create gpu-ephemeral-west1c --cluster=prod-cluster --zone=us-west1-c --machine-type=n1-standard-16 --accelerator type=nvidia-t4,count=1 --node-labels=gpu.family=t4,pool=ephemeral --num-nodes=0 --enable-autoscaling --min-nodes=0 --max-nodes=10```
carla: Add `--image-type=UBUNTU` and `--metadata=install-nvidia-driver=true` so we don't wait on driver bootstrap.
jin: While that's spinning up, we should also enable `kube-scheduler` cross-pool prioritization: add `topology.kubernetes.io/zone` acceptableDuringScheduling to the affinity so pods can prefer zone-b but accept c.
oncall-ops: k8s-autoscaler-bot: `Nodepool gpu-ephemeral-west1c created (0 -> 0). Autoscaler active. Recommended scale: 3 nodes`
alex: Runbook question — do we want automatic eviction of lower-priority spot GPUs when we need to scale reserved? Current policy is reverse.
maya: We recently updated policies: `spot->reserved` eviction is enabled for 15m window. We can temporarily flip it with `kubectl patch` to increase reserved pool priority. But that is manual and risky for customer workloads.
sam: Suggestion: enable immediate taint-based preemption only for realtime pods: add `PreferNoSchedule` -> `NoSchedule` on spot pool for label `realtime=true` and then cordon/uncordon when capacity recovers.
carla: That needs coordination with control-plane and also affects rolling upgrades. Not ideal mid-day.
jin: Another angle — route some realtime traffic to our dedicated cluster in us-central1 for a few hours using traffic routing policy. Network latency might increase ~20ms though. Is that acceptable for the SLO?
alex: Realtime SLO is p95 < 120ms end-to-end. us-central1 adds ~25ms median — borderline. We can send only burst/failsafe requests there.
maya: Ops play: 1) spin up us-west1-c nodepool (ephemeral) 2) bump autoscaler max for that pool to +10 3) temporarily demote P2 to CPU 4) monitor queue depth + tail latency 5) notify finance if on-demand needed >4 hours.
sam: I'll create a small k8s job to patch P2 deployments to `nodeSelector: cpu-fallback=true` and add `replicas: same` so it drains GPU queue. Command: ```kubectl set env deployment/rerank RERANK_MODE=cpu --namespace=ml-batch```
oncall-ops: k8s-autoscaler-bot: `Scaling action: gpu-ephemeral-west1c +3 nodes (creating). Expected ready: ~7m`
carla: Watch for image pulls and NV driver install delays. If nodes are not Ready in >10m, we might need to use a node image prebuilt with drivers.
jin: If driver time is the blocker, we can trigger a `DaemonSet` that installs but better to have them baked. Use `gcloud` node image `cos_gpu` in future.
maya: Initial nodes are coming up. I'm also opening a quick PR to autoscaler creds team so it can request quota bump temporary.
alex: For postmortem, capture: zone capacity, spot eviction patterns, image-mirror absence in the new zone, decision timeline, cost incurred. Assign owners?
sam: I'll own the technical mitigation (nodepool + affinity). maya take financial comms and nodepool ops. carla document runbook updates. jin coordinate routing fallback to central cluster.
maya: Ack. I'll send a short status to #incidents with ETA 15m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
oncall-ops: k8s-autoscaler-bot: `gpu-ephemeral-west1c nodes ready: 3. Autoscaler stable.`
alex: Confirming: Pending queue drained, p95 latency stable at 98ms now. Thanks team. Let's follow up on bake images + automated cross-zone mirror work next week.
carla: Noted — will add a checklist to the infra runbook for "ephemeral cross-zone GPU spillover": image mirror, baked GPU image, autocrank autoscaler quotas, taint toggles.
jin: Also add an evaluation for regional routing policy thresholds so we can programmatically route bursts to dedicated clusters before manual ops.
maya: Closing this thread, creating follow-ups in taskboard. :white_check_mark:
